item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 2, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's what's happening across the media industry.
Media Jobs Report welcomes radio sales expert Harmony Tenney as its newest Pro Member. With more than 20 years of experience, Tenney is a sales coach, consultant and author of the newly released Ultimate Radio Sales Playbook, featuring 60 chapters designed to help radio sales professionals close more deals, strengthen client relationships and increase commissions. Join the Media Jobs Report Pro Network. Explore the benefits of a Pro Membership at Media Jobs Report dot com.
In public media news,
Public television is mourning Beth Courtney, the former President and CEO of Louisiana Public Broadcasting. Courtney made history in 1985 as the first woman to lead a statewide public broadcasting network. During her 36-year tenure, LPB expanded to seven stations and affiliates. America’s Public Television Stations praised her decades of leadership and lasting contributions to public media.
Also making news,
The FCC says its crackdown on fraud and waste has resulted in billions of dollars in recovered funds, avoided spending and money returned to the Treasury. Chairman Brendan Carr reports nearly four billion dollars returned, 160 million in fines and recoveries, and almost 300 million illegal robocalls blocked. Additional enforcement actions and regulatory reforms are planned.
Turning to radio,
Cumulus Media is bringing ZoneCasting technology to Boston’s 104.5 XLO in early 2027. The system will let advertisers air different commercials simultaneously in specific geographic areas, beginning east of Route 128. Combined with Xperi’s DTS AutoStage listening data, the technology could give radio advertisers more precise audience targeting while maintaining FM radio’s broad reach.
On the business side of media,
Nexstar Media Group has declared a quarterly cash dividend of one dollar and eighty-six cents per share. The dividend will be paid November twenty-seventh to shareholders of record as of November thirteenth. Nexstar says it plans to continue quarterly dividends, subject to Board approval.
Elsewhere in public broadcasting,
NPR has named David Berzin Senior Vice President of Product and Data. Berzin joins from Hearst Magazines, where he led international product development and artificial intelligence initiatives. He previously held digital leadership roles at Viacom and MTV. At NPR, Berzin will oversee digital products, audience engagement and data strategy, helping strengthen connections with listeners and member stations while supporting new revenue opportunities.
And finally,
iHeartRadio and TikTok LIVE are teaming up with Latin music star Anuel AA for an exclusive album preview November fifth. Hosted by iHeartLatino President Enrique Santos, the livestream will feature new music and the release date announcement for Real Hasta La Muerte 2. The special begins at seven Eastern on TikTok, with radio broadcasts planned for the album's release day.
Stay current with more media news, the latest jobs and free industry tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
